questions.q: Thornbury Cycle Supply Co.'s "QBR package" request actually breaks into how many separate deliverables, and why?
options: One deliverable, since a QBR is always a single dashboard
Three deliverables — Power BI for Executives, Tableau for the Board, Excel for Finance — because each audience consumes numbers differently
Two deliverables — one for internal staff, one for external parties
Four deliverables, one per quarter of the fiscal year
questions.explain: Executives want an interactive Power BI dashboard, the Board wants a polished, presentation-ready Tableau deck, and Finance wants an Excel workbook they can manipulate with their own formulas — three genuinely different jobs-to-be-done.

questions.q: Why does Finance specifically ask for an Excel workbook instead of a BI tool?
options: Because Excel is cheaper than Power BI or Tableau
Because Finance wants numbers they can pull apart, re-sum, and audit with their own formulas before signing off
Because Finance doesn't have access to Power BI
Because Excel loads data faster than a BI tool
questions.explain: Finance's whole job-to-be-done is auditing a number, not just viewing it — a workbook they can manipulate directly with formulas like SUMIFS serves that better than a locked BI dashboard.

questions.q: Why is building three independent front-ends normally considered risky, and what does this capstone do to prevent that risk?
options: It isn't risky at all, since each tool is built by a different team
Three front-ends each querying their own copy of the data can quietly disagree; this capstone has all three read from one shared dw.* warehouse instead
It's risky only if the company uses more than one cloud provider
The risk is eliminated by using the same color palette in all three tools
questions.explain: The only way three independently built deliverables can agree with each other is to build them all on top of the exact same underlying numbers — one warehouse, read by three front-ends, never from each other.

questions.q: What is the real, underlying source system for every number this capstone produces?
options: A spreadsheet of made-up sample figures
The real AdventureWorks2012 OLTP sample database
A third-party market research report
Thornbury's point-of-sale terminals, queried live
questions.explain: Every deliverable traces back to real rows in AdventureWorks2012 — tables like Sales.SalesOrderHeader, Sales.SalesOrderDetail, and Production.Product.

questions.q: What two layers sit underneath the three front-end tools in this capstone's architecture?
options: A new dw.* T-SQL warehouse, and an automated Python data-quality validation layer
A second OLTP database, and a manual nightly spreadsheet audit
A caching layer and a load balancer
A backup database and an email alert system
questions.explain: The warehouse is the shared source of truth all three front-ends read from, and the Python validation layer catches data-quality problems before any front-end ever sees them.
